meta.subtitle: Third kit: 24x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 (1.5 TB, single lot) - Tyrone MDA200A2N-224
meta.platform: Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 / 2x AMD EPYC 9135 (32C/64T, Zen 5 Turin)

executive_summary: Post-install revalidation of the third DIMM kit fitted to server 172.16.11.132 today (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135). All 24x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 modules train at full rated speed on a clean POST: no ACPI BERT error records and no BMC 'Memory Device Disabled' events on the current boot - unlike the previous kit, whose two failed modules were mapped out every boot. Full 1.5 TB usable, symmetric 12+12 channels (1 DPC). The kit is a single uniform lot (80CE04254742Exxxxx) with zero serial overlap with both kits tested earlier today.

The 5-minute 100% burn held 1388 GB (92% of RAM) resident across 64 verify-mode workers and completed 1.58 billion verified operations (the highest of today's three runs) with zero failures, zero OOM/swap; EDAC CE=0/UE=0, zero machine-checks, zero new SEL entries during the campaign; cores held full boost (peak 4341 MHz vs 4300 rated).

Bandwidth is back at baseline parity: 567.5 GB/s aggregate stream = 98% of this morning's 24-DIMM baseline (581.1 GB/s, within run-to-run variance) and +63% over the failed asymmetric kit (348.6 GB/s); DRAM-bound sysbench read/write land at 101%/99% of baseline. Single-thread memcpy 24.2 GB/s and NUMA-remote ratio 1.63x are nominal. The configuration is qualified for production memory-bound workloads.

comparison.caption: Same server, same day, same tooling - third kit vs this morning's 24-DIMM baseline kit. All metrics at parity (within run-to-run variance).
comparison.notes: Full symmetric 12+12-channel population restores the interleave: 567.5 GB/s aggregate is 98% of the baseline kit and +63% over the intermediate failed kit (348.6 GB/s, 22 DIMMs asymmetric). sysbench read/write land at 101%/99% of baseline; single-thread memcpy and the NUMA-remote ratio are nominal. Today's three same-day runs cleanly demonstrate: full population = ~570-580 GB/s, losing one channel per socket = -40%.

sel_status: BMC SEL: 0 new entries during the campaign (342 before and after; last entry 09:46 UTC, pre-test boot). The 19 entries added during the swap session (323 -> 342) are: one 09:29 boot that still carried the previous kit's two 'Memory Device Disabled' map-outs, then PSU AC-loss/presence + chassis-intrusion artifacts at 09:33 (benign - AC pulled during physical work), and a clean 09:44/09:46 boot with NO memory events for the current kit.
dmesg_status: Clean POST for this kit: ACPI BERT is empty on the current boot (no error records ingested - the previous kit logged fatal map-out records every boot). During the campaign: 0 machine-check events, AMD EDAC CE=0/UE=0 on both controllers, core clocks 4051-4341 MHz under load, swap untouched, no OOM-killer activity.
findings: All 24 modules of the third kit train at full 5600 MT/s on a clean POST: no ACPI BERT error records and no BMC 'Memory Device Disabled' events on the current boot - full 1.5 TB usable on symmetric 12+12 channels. This directly clears the failure mode of the previous kit (2 modules mapped out with DRAM storage errors).

Aggregate bandwidth is restored to baseline parity: 567.5 GB/s (98% of this morning's 581.1 GB/s on the original kit; the 2% delta is run-to-run variance) and +63% over the failed asymmetric kit. DRAM-bound sysbench: read 360.8 GB/s (101% of baseline), write 204.0 GB/s (99%).

The 5-minute 100% burn is spotless: 1388 GB (92% of RAM) resident for the entire window, 1,576,209,418 verified operations (the highest count of today's three runs) with zero failures, zero OOM, swap untouched; EDAC CE=0/UE=0; zero machine-checks; zero new SEL entries.
Single-thread and NUMA behavior nominal: 24.2 GB/s 1-thread memcpy, node0->node0 23.1 GiB/s vs node0->node1 14.2 GiB/s = 1.63x remote penalty (family norm 1.6-1.7x).

Kit identity recorded for traceability: third distinct set today, zero serial overlap with both prior kits; all 24 modules from one uniform lot (80CE04254742Exxxxx) - single-lot population is the preferred configuration for timing margin. Full slot-by-slot serial map in the Hardware Inventory section.

Today's three same-day campaigns on this box now form a complete lot-acceptance record: Run 1 (original kit) PASS at 581 GB/s; Run 2 (second kit) FAIL - 2 modules mapped out, asymmetric 11+11 channels, -40% bandwidth; Run 3 (this kit) PASS at 567.5 GB/s.
recommendations: Kit qualified for production: 24/24 trained, baseline-parity bandwidth, zero errors across burn and benchmarks - cleared for memory-bound workloads (in-memory DBs, virtualization, HPC pre/post-processing).

Process the removed second kit: RMA the two modules from positions P0 CH-C and P1 CH-L (BERT 'Storage error in DRAM memory' is a module-internal failure signature; record label serials - SPD was not readable while mapped out). The other 22 modules of that kit tested electrically clean and can return to spares.
Install rasdaemon and enable BIOS patrol scrub before production so any in-service DIMM degradation is logged per-DIMM.
Optional: run the 3-hour qualification tier (memtester near-full-residency burn + extended soak, as on .41/.217) before final customer handover.
Archive today's three reports together (Run 1 PASS / Run 2 FAIL / Run 3 PASS) as the acceptance record for this server's memory configuration history.
